grade.first_issue: The necessity argument in Section 4 is unsupported, invoking Rule E. Since Mulan may choose the cut parameter continuously, newly created angles are not confined to the asserted countable family \(\phi+m\theta+k180^\circ\). Merely choosing an initial triangle outside a countable set provides no strategy ensuring that Shan-Yu can keep avoiding \(\theta\) after every future cut.
grade.summary: The final classification is correct, and the peeling construction gives substantial progress toward sufficiency. However, the entire only-if direction depends on an invalid countability assertion and supplies neither the required invariant nor an adaptive safe-child strategy for Shan-Yu. Establishing necessity requires a genuinely new central argument, so the proof is capped at 3 by Rule E.
strengths: Correctly identifies the answer \(\theta=180^\circ/n\) for integers \(n\ge2\).
The angle-peeling move from \(m\theta\) to \((m-1)\theta\) is essentially correct.
Move B is a viable basis for sufficiency once its ordering and legality conditions are supplied.

errors.description: The claimed restriction of all creatable angles to a countable affine family is undefined or false: a cut can introduce an arbitrary real angle. Consequently, the countability argument does not prove that any starting triangle is unwinnable.
No invariant is proved showing that for every Mulan cut Shan-Yu has a child that remains safe. This is the decisive missing necessity argument.

For \(\theta<60^\circ\), the statement that repeated Move A creates an angle below \(\theta\) is not explained, though it is readily repaired by repeatedly subtracting \(\theta\) from an angle initially exceeding \(\theta\).
Move B requires not only \(\gamma<\theta\) but also a suitable ordering ensuring \(\alpha+\gamma>\theta\); the proof does not specify choosing \(\alpha\) as the larger remaining angle.
